facts.fact_text: According to the applicants, in the period from 20 May to 6 July 2010 they participated in protest activities against a road-construction project in Gorky Park (Парк ім. Горького) in Kharkiv.
According to the applicants, the protest activities in Gorky Park included obstructing tree-felling work.
Some protesters actively attempted to interfere with the tree-felling work in Gorky Park by climbing trees with the help of climbing equipment and attaching themselves to the trees to be felled.
Some protesters interfered with work to be carried out by machinery by placing themselves in front of it.
Notwithstanding the protests, the tree-felling and construction work in Gorky Park proceeded.
According to the Government's submissions, in response to the protesters' actions the security guards attempted to drive them away by pushing them back beyond the boundaries of the construction area.
In some instances, clashes took place between security guards and protesters in Gorky Park.
On at least fifteen occasions ambulances were called to the Gorky Park construction site during the protest events.
The bulk of the protest activity in Gorky Park was brought to an end on 2 June 2010 and most of the protesters left the site on that day.
Some protesters apparently continued to picket the Gorky Park construction site until about mid-August 2010.

One issue raised in connection with the Gorky Park events is whether the arrest and conviction of the first six applicants for refusal to obey orders to leave the construction site breached their freedom of peaceful assembly.
Regarding the arrest and conviction issue, the first five applicants were arrested together, forming one sub-group.
Regarding the arrest and conviction issue, the sixth applicant was arrested on a different date from the first five applicants, forming a separate sub-group.
On 28 May 2010 the first to fifth, the eighth and the tenth applicants, among other protesters, were arrested and taken to a police station.

At the police station on 28 May 2010, charges of malicious insubordination in the face of lawful demands of a police officer were drawn up against the first to fifth, the eighth and the tenth applicants.

According to the offence reports drawn up on 28 May 2010, the arrested applicants had repeatedly refused to abide by police officers' instructions to leave the construction site and resisted the officers' efforts to remove them, in particular by dragging their feet and attempting to break free and to remain on the site.
It appears that the first to fifth, the eighth and the tenth applicants were released shortly after the offence reports had been drawn up on 28 May 2010.
The applicants submitted that the construction site had no boundary markers and they had believed that they were lawfully in a public open space.
The applicants submitted that about 100 police officers had been standing nearby and had never asked the protesters to leave the area.
The applicants submitted that a number of men in black with Municipal Guard (MG) badges had surrounded the protesters and started pressing them into a tight circle.

The applicants submitted that police officers had then approached and, instead of responding to the protesters' cries for help, had taken some of the protesters, including the applicants, out of the crowd one by one and escorted them to the police station, without any demands or explanations.
The applicants submitted that they had followed the police officers without offering any resistance.

In his statement to the police the first applicant said that at 7.30 a.m. on 28 May 2010 he had been in Gorky Park with his bicycle, had been grabbed by people with Municipal Guard (MG) badges and then handed over to the police.

In his statement to the police the second applicant said that at 7.20 a.m. on 28 May 2010 he had been in Gorky Park near the railway crossing, had seen a crowd and come closer to find out what was going on, and had been unaware that construction work was being conducted there.

The second applicant stated to the police that individuals with Municipal Guard (MG) badges had pushed him and others away from the railway crossing and encircled them, after which police officers had come and dragged him out of the circle and to the police station, and that he had not heard any warnings to leave the site.

At the hearing on 9 June 2010 the Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court also heard the first and second applicants and some witnesses, and examined the video recording submitted by the applicants' lawyer.
At the close of the hearing on 9 June 2010 the Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court convicted the first and second applicants as charged and sentenced them to fifteen days' administrative detention.

The Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court stated that, in view of the examined evidence including that submitted by the defence, it was convinced that the first and second applicants were guilty as charged.

The first and second applicants' lawyer argued on appeal that the Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court had failed to set out its analysis of the evidence which had led it to the conclusion that the applicants were guilty, and had thus failed adequately to reason its judgments.
On 18 June 2010 the Kharkiv Regional Court of Appeal upheld the conviction of the first and second applicants.

In the course of the hearing before the Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court, the third applicant stated that he had indeed been in Gorky Park, had not heard any orders to leave the site from the police officers but had heard it from a person in civilian clothing, and had been dragged from the circle by police officers who had taken him to the police station.
On 14 June 2010 the Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court, having heard the police officers, the third and fourth applicants and some witnesses, convicted the third and fourth applicants as charged.
The Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court sentenced the third applicant to a fine of 136 Ukrainian hryvnias (UAH), at the time the equivalent of about 14 euros (EUR).
The Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court sentenced the fourth applicant to a fine of 170 Ukrainian hryvnias (UAH), at the time the equivalent of about 17 euros (EUR).

On 23 June 2010 the Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court, having heard the police officers, the fifth applicant and some witnesses, convicted the fifth applicant as charged and fined him 170 Ukrainian hryvnias (UAH), at the time the equivalent of about 17 euros (EUR).

On 27 July 2010 the Kharkiv Regional Court of Appeal quashed the fifth applicant's conviction by a final decision and discontinued the proceedings against the fifth applicant under Article 22 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1984.
On 8 June 2010 the Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court discontinued proceedings against the eighth applicant.
On 12 July 2010 the Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court discontinued proceedings against the tenth applicant.
On 6 July 2010 the sixth applicant was arrested and charged with malicious insubordination in the face of orders given by police officers to leave the construction site in Gorky Park.
On 7 July 2010 the sixth applicant's case was heard by the Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court, at which the police officers supported the charges.
At the hearing on 7 July 2010 the sixth applicant acknowledged that he had been sitting on the ground in the construction area, protesting against the tree felling, which he considered unlawful.

The sixth applicant acknowledged that he had refused to comply with the police officers' requests to leave the construction site, to the point where they had had to drag him away by the arms with his legs dragging on the ground.
On 7 July 2010 the Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court convicted the sixth applicant as charged and sentenced him to ten days' administrative detention.

In justifying the sanction imposed on the sixth applicant, the Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court stated that it had taken into account the nature of the offence and its specific circumstances, the applicant's personal characteristics, the fact that he had no employment, the absence of aggravating or attenuating circumstances, and the need to re-educate the offender and to prevent new offences.

The Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court considered that the use of sanctions less severe than imprisonment would be insufficient and that administrative detention needed to be imposed on the sixth applicant, but not for the maximum duration provided for in the law.

The decision of 9 August 2010 described the events of 28 May 2010 as follows: at around 7 a.m. the Main Contractor's staff had marked the boundaries of the construction site with tape and Municipal Guard (MG) staff had taken up the duties of guarding it.

According to the decision of 9 August 2010, the Municipal Guard (MG) staff had asked individuals who were within the perimeter to leave the area in order to avoid the risk of trauma from the construction equipment, and when they refused, the Main Contractor's management had appealed to the police for help in removing those individuals from the construction site.
According to the decision of 9 August 2010, some protesters had then been arrested as they had refused to leave the construction site on 28 May 2010.
Private security company PS staff had provided guard services on the Gorky Park construction site from 28 May to 2 June 2010.

When questioned, the private security company PS guards stated that they had avoided any conflict with the protesters and had not assaulted them, despite provocative behaviour on the part of the latter.

On 26 May 2010 the Regional Architecture and Construction Inspectorate (Інспекція державного архітектурно-будівельного контролю у Харківській області) issued to the Kharkiv Municipal Construction Department a permit to carry out preparatory work for the road construction.
Under the agreement between the Main Contractor and Municipal Guard (MG), MG undertook to provide services consisting of guarding the road construction site in Gorky Park.
MG held a licence authorising it to provide commercial security guard services, issued on 2 February 2010 by the Ministry of the Interior.
On 19 May 2010 Kharkiv city police approved an action plan for ensuring public safety during the tree-felling work in Gorky Park.
According to the Kharkiv city police action plan of 19 May 2010, twenty-seven active officers were assigned for ensuring public order and safety at the construction site daily from 20 May 2010.

The Kharkiv city police action plan of 19 May 2010 mentioned that the tree felling could potentially generate picketing, demonstrations and other unexpected action by opponents of the construction project.

The subject of the agreement between the Main Contractor and private security company PS was the provision of security guard services for the purpose of preventing third parties from entering the road construction site in Gorky Park.
The security guard services provided by private security company PS were to be provided as from 28 May 2010.
Private security company PS held a licence authorising it to provide commercial security guard services, issued on 11 April 2007 by the Ministry of the Interior.

On 25 May 2010 the Main Contractor asked the chief of the Kharkiv city police to send police units to the construction site at 7 a.m. on 26 May 2010 to prevent third parties from infiltrating the construction site.
On 29 May 2010 the Main Contractor asked the chief of police of the then Dzerzhinsky (presently Shevchenkivsky) District, where Gorky Park is located, to ensure public order on the construction site.

The Main Contractor's request of 29 May 2010 referred to an incident the previous day in which, according to the company, unidentified people had interfered with the construction work, shouted profanities at the workers and tried to provoke a fight.

Cabinet of Ministers Resolution no. 1045 of 1 August 2006 stipulated that trees could be removed within the framework of implementation of urban development plans but that their removal required a decision by the executive authority of the municipality and an order, and that before any decision could be issued, the trees had to be examined by a commission appointed by the municipal authorities.

At the material time, safety rules for construction were contained in Construction Norms and Rules (СНиП) III-4-80 Safety Rules for Construction, enacted by Order no. 82 of the USSR State Committee on Construction of 9 June 1980, which continued to be applicable in Ukraine on the basis of Resolution of the Ukrainian Parliament of 12 September 1991 on temporary application of legislative acts of the Soviet Union.
Rule 1.16 of Construction Norms and Rules III-4-80 prohibited access of unauthorised persons to construction sites.

Article 32 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1984 provides that administrative detention for up to fifteen days may be applied by courts only in exceptional cases for certain administrative offences.

Article 185 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1984 provides that malicious disobedience in the face of a lawful order or demand by a police officer who is carrying out his official duties shall be punished by a fine of between 136 and 255 Ukrainian hryvnias (UAH), or by withholding 20% of earnings; or, in the event that in the particular circumstances of the case and with regard to the offender's character these measures are found to be insufficient, by administrative detention of up to fifteen days.

Article 185-1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1984 provides that a breach of the procedure for organising and holding meetings, rallies, street marches and demonstrations shall be punishable by a reprimand or by a fine, and that the same actions committed within a year of the application of administrative penalties or by the organiser shall be punishable by a fine, or by correctional labour of one to two months with a deduction of 20% of earnings, or by administrative detention of up to fifteen days.

The Kharkiv city police action plan of 19 May 2010 mentioned that the tree felling could potentially generate picketing, demonstrations and other unexpected action by opponents of the construction project.

The police chief's report of 3 June 2010 stated that police officers had been deployed in full force as envisaged by the law-enforcement plan, that is twenty-seven officers on site daily from 20 May to 2 June 2010, except for 23, 29 and 30 May 2010 when two officers had been deployed.
The police chief's report of 3 June 2010 stated that the construction site had been marked off with tape on 28 May 2010.
The police chief's report of 3 June 2010 stated that the picketing of the construction site had been discontinued at 9.45 a.m. on 2 June 2010.

At the close of the hearing on 9 June 2010 the Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court convicted the first and second applicants as charged and sentenced them to fifteen days' administrative detention.

The Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court stated that, in view of the examined evidence including that submitted by the defence, it was convinced that the first and second applicants were guilty as charged.

The Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court stated that having examined the circumstances of the case and the character of the first and second applicants, it was convinced that a punishment less severe than detention would not be adequate.
The Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court's decision convicting the first and second applicants was enforced immediately and the applicants were taken into custody.
On 18 June 2010 the Kharkiv Regional Court of Appeal upheld the conviction of the first and second applicants.
The Kharkiv Regional Court of Appeal found that the case-file material showed that the police officers had acted lawfully in directing the first and second applicants to leave the construction site.
The Kharkiv Regional Court of Appeal found that the construction work was being conducted on the basis of valid permits and the appellants had failed to show otherwise.

The Kharkiv Regional Court of Appeal concluded that the Kharkiv Dzerzhinsky District Court had not had sufficient grounds to impose the maximum punishment on the first and second applicants, having failed to sufficiently take into account the circumstances of the cases and the applicants' personal characteristics.
The Kharkiv Regional Court of Appeal reduced the first and second applicants' sentence from fifteen days to nine days' detention.
On 18 June 2010 the Kharkiv Regional Court of Appeal's decision became final and the first and second applicants were released.

Article 22 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1984 provides that in the case of an offence of minor importance the offender could be relieved of liability with a reprimand.

Article 32 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1984 provides that administrative detention for up to fifteen days may be applied by courts only in exceptional cases for certain administrative offences.

Article 33 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1984 requires the sentencing authority, in determining a sentence, to take into account the nature of the offence in question, the degree of culpability of the person concerned and his or her financial situation, and any attenuating and aggravating circumstances.

The applicants alleged a number of attacks on them and other protesters by the security guards and loggers in the period from 20 May to 2 June 2010 in Gorky Park.
According to the applicants, on 27 May 2010 the ninth applicant was beaten by unidentified men in orange vests.
An ambulance was called following the alleged beating of the ninth applicant on 27 May 2010 and the ninth applicant was taken to hospital.
The ninth applicant was diagnosed at hospital as having sustained injuries to the soft tissue of the head and face and was treated as an outpatient.
On 27 May 2010 the ninth applicant lodged a complaint with the district police, alleging that he had been assaulted in the course of the Gorky Park events near the children's railway.
According to the applicants, on 31 May 2010 the seventh applicant was assaulted by men in black wearing Municipal Guard (MG) badges in response to her protests about the beating of another protester.
According to the seventh applicant, police officers who were standing nearby on 31 May 2010 observed the assault on her without reacting to her cries for help.
On 31 May 2010 the seventh applicant was taken to hospital by ambulance.
The seventh applicant was diagnosed at hospital on 31 May 2010 as suffering from stress-related hypertension and soft tissue contusions in the lumbar area.
The seventh applicant stayed in hospital on 31 May 2010 from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.
On 1 June 2010 the seventh applicant complained to the head of the Dzerzhinsky District police that on 31 May 2010 she had been hit in the back by Municipal Guard (MG) staff.

Video and photographic material for 31 May 2010 shows a tumultuous scene with men in black with badges confronting a large group of individuals in civilian clothing, pulling some protesters away from an area they are attempting to protect, and then forming an elbow-to-elbow line blocking access.
Video material for 31 May 2010 shows individuals in civilian clothing on the protesters' side filming the events, with shouts of 'Police!' and 'Call an ambulance!'
Video material for 31 May 2010 shows a woman (apparently the seventh applicant) lying on the ground surrounded by the crowd, after which an ambulance team arrives and takes her away.

Photographs for 31 May 2010 show individuals apparently protesters sitting in groups around trees marked with slogans, men in black clothing with badges confronting individuals in civilian clothing and pushing them away, and a man in black facing what appears to be a group of protesters sitting on the ground and holding onto a tree.
According to the applicants, on 2 June 2010 men in black with Municipal Guard (MG) badges and loggers were attempting to clear the Gorky Park construction site of protesters.
According to the applicants, on 2 June 2010 the third applicant was closely approached by two loggers, subsequently identified as A. and K., employees of one of the subcontractors.

According to the applicants, on 2 June 2010 loggers A. and K. threatened the third applicant and a group of other protesters with working chainsaws, and one of them nearly injured the third applicant.
The Government alleged that on 2 June 2010 it was the protesters who had attacked the workers, trying to take away the chainsaws, so that the workers had had to retreat to avoid injuries.

In their statements in the course of the domestic investigation, as summarised in the decision not to institute criminal proceedings of 9 August 2010, loggers A. and K. stated that on 2 June 2010, on arriving at the designated felling area in Gorky Park, they had observed men in black and protesters.
Loggers A. and K. stated that the protesters had started insulting the workers and the men in black, then started to push A. and K., grabbing their arms and trying to seize their chainsaws.

Loggers A. and K. stated that in order to prevent people from approaching, they had switched on the chainsaws, but the protesters had started approaching and in order not to injure them, A. and K. had had to step back, holding the chainsaws in front of them.

Video material for 2 June 2010 shows a tumultuous scene involving dozens of individuals, with men in black attempting to push the protesters away from the trees and the protesters attempting to hold their ground and push back, while several police officers observe.
Video material for 2 June 2010 shows two workers starting their chainsaws some distance away from the main altercation.

Video material for 2 June 2010 shows an individual identified as the third applicant approaching closely and confronting one of the workers with running chainsaws, raising and spreading his arms, with several other individuals also closely approaching the worker.
Video material for 2 June 2010 shows the worker stepping back while holding the chainsaw close and waving it in horizontal semi-circles in front of him.
Video material for 2 June 2010 shows a group of individuals in camouflage and in black intervening and interposing themselves in a line between the workers and the protesters.

On 28 May 2010 the cases against the first and second applicants were sent to court.
The first and second applicants requested that the hearings in their cases be postponed as they needed time to appoint a lawyer, and they appointed a lawyer on 28 May 2010.

On various dates the protesters, including some of the applicants, complained to the law-enforcement authorities that they had been assaulted by unidentified loggers and men in black clothing with Municipal Guard (MG) badges.
The protesters' complaints to law-enforcement authorities also alleged that the police officers stationed nearby had done nothing to protect them during the Gorky Park events.
The protesters' complaints were investigated by the Kharkiv city prosecutor's office.

The police chief's report of 3 June 2010 stated that the picketing of the construction site had been discontinued at 9.45 a.m. on 2 June 2010.
The Kharkiv city prosecutor's office questioned a number of police officers, employees of subcontractor companies, and journalists in the course of its investigation.

In November 2010 a number of protesters, including all the applicants, lodged an action with the Kharkiv Circuit Administrative Court, complaining that the police had failed to protect them against assaults during their peaceful protest against the tree felling, in particular on 28 and 31 May and 1 and 2 June 2010.

According to the Government, in the course of the trial before the Kharkiv Circuit Administrative Court, the seventh applicant was examined by a representative of the police and stated that she could not say with certitude who had hit her on 31 May 2010 and only supposed that it had been a person in black.
On 24 May 2011 the Kharkiv Circuit Administrative Court rejected the applicants' claim that the police had failed to protect them against assaults during their protest.
On 9 December 2011 the Kharkiv Administrative Court of Appeal upheld the Kharkiv Circuit Administrative Court's decision of 24 May 2011.

On 26 June 2014 the High Administrative Court allowed an appeal lodged by the applicants and remitted the case to the Kharkiv Circuit Administrative Court for re-examination on the grounds that the lower courts' examination of the facts had been incomplete.

The High Administrative Court found that the lower courts had failed, in particular, to establish whether attacks on the protesters had really taken place, the list of the officers present, and whether the protesters had appealed for help.

As of 8 October 2014, the date of the last communication from the applicants on this point, the applicants' claim concerning the police's failure to protect them was pending before the Kharkiv Circuit Administrative Court.
